parent_v13.key_result: all declared topology-sensitive targets were exactly resolvable in 144 twelve-world random panels, usually with three and occasionally four fixed REL/FP/KO measurements

scientific_question: Can exact outcome-adaptive relational measurement reduce the information burden for topology-sensitive ecological targets relative to the best fixed nonadaptive measurement panel in random static-equivalent worlds?

analysis_base.worlds: exact frozen v12 random static-equivalent topology worlds
analysis_base.atomic_measurements: exact unchanged v13 REL, FP and KO measurements only

adaptive_planner.state: current surviving subset of the 12 topology worlds
adaptive_planner.target_stop_rule: stop as soon as all surviving worlds share the declared target value; full world identity is not required unless the target is full_topology_identity
adaptive_planner.action_outcome: the exact deterministic v13 measurement value in the realized world
adaptive_planner.transition: retain worlds with the observed measurement value
adaptive_planner.objective: minimize worst-case number of additional measurements to target identification
adaptive_planner.exact_solver: memoized recursion over active-world subsets; actions that do not split the current subset are skipped
adaptive_planner.tie_rule: lexicographically smallest action ID among equal worst-case depths
adaptive_planner.repeated_action_rule: no explicit remaining-action state is needed because a deterministic action already observed on a branch is constant within that child subset and cannot split it again

nonadaptive_reference: the exact fixed minimum measurement count already frozen in v13 for the same row and target

secondary_uniform_world_summary.definition: mean realized depth of the canonical worst-case-optimal adaptive policy when each of the 12 declared worlds is counted once with equal weight
secondary_uniform_world_summary.claim_boundary: descriptive finite-panel average only; not an ecological prior or expected utility

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: For every row and target, exact adaptive worst-case depth is <= the v13 exact fixed nonadaptive minimum measurement count.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any violation is an implementation/theory failure.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one row-target combination has adaptive worst-case depth strictly smaller than its v13 fixed minimum.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if adaptive and fixed worst-case burdens are identical everywhere.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: For each of pairwise_relation, first_passage and intervention, at least one row has canonical-policy mean realized depth strictly below the fixed minimum.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED separately for any target lacking such a row.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Within every row, adaptive worst-case depth for pairwise_relation, first_passage, intervention and critical_node_count is <= adaptive depth for full_topology_identity.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any violation is an implementation/theory failure.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: For intervention or critical_node_count, at least one row has adaptive worst-case depth strictly below full_topology_identity depth.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if neither narrow target ever saves a worst-case measurement.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one row-target optimal adaptive tree chooses different second actions after different first-action outcomes.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if every exact optimal policy is effectively one fixed measurement order.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Across row-target canonical adaptive policies, more than one distinct first action ID occurs.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if one fixed measurement is canonical first everywhere.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Every row resolves all 12 topology identities under the unchanged REL/FP/KO library.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if any row is adaptively unresolved for full topology identity.

secondary_outputs: adaptive worst-case depth distributions by target and active-node count
number of branching policies and branch-specific second-action diversity
rows where target planner stops with multiple topology worlds
relationship between v13 fixed burden and adaptive saving
claim_boundary: Adaptive depths are finite decision-tree information counts, not field sampling costs.
The equal-world mean realized depth is not an ecological probability model.
Outcome-adaptive target identification does not imply historical truth when multiple worlds share the target.
No novelty is claimed for generic adaptive decision trees; the ecological question is how much relational evidence the EOG topology targets require.
stop_rules: Do not add raw-edge queries after scoring.
Do not add measurement families beyond REL/FP/KO.
Do not change action costs after scoring.
Do not switch from worst-case to expected-depth optimization after scoring.
Do not drop rows where adaptation gives no saving.
